scenario:
Seven performers — Adler, Brennan, Cortez, Doshi, Espinoza, Farrow, and Gaines — will each take the stage exactly once during a recital, in seven consecutive time slots numbered 1 through 7. Each performer occupies exactly one slot, and each slot is occupied by exactly one performer. The following constraints apply:
1. Adler performs before Brennan.
2. Cortez performs in slot 3 or slot 5.
3. Doshi performs immediately before or immediately after Espinoza.
4. Farrow does not perform in slot 1 or slot 7.
5. If Gaines performs in slot 1, then Adler performs in slot 2.

rules.note: Cortez performs in slot 3 or slot 5

explanations.correct: Brennan must always perform in slot 6 or slot 7. Because Adler must perform before Brennan (Rule 1), Brennan cannot occupy any slot that would leave no room for Adler ahead of it — but more decisively, Cortez anchors slot 3 or 5, Doshi and Espinoza occupy two adjacent slots, and Farrow is excluded from slots 1 and 7. Working through every valid arrangement, Brennan is always pushed to slot 6 or 7. No valid solution places Brennan in slots 1–5.
explanations.A: False in arrangements where Cortez is in slot 3 and Adler is in slot 4 or later. Adler need not precede Cortez.
explanations.B: Farrow can appear in slots 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6. Farrow is not locked to slot 6 in all valid arrangements.
explanations.C: Correct. In every valid arrangement satisfying all five rules, Brennan lands in slot 6 or slot 7.
explanations.D: Gaines can perform in slot 7 in multiple valid arrangements (e.g., when Adler is in slot 1 and Gaines finishes last), so this is not necessarily true.
explanations.E: Doshi need not precede Cortez; in arrangements where Cortez is in slot 3 and the Doshi–Espinoza block occupies slots 4–5 or 5–6, Cortez precedes Doshi.

explanations.correct: With Cortez in slot 5 and Farrow in slot 6, the remaining performers — Adler, Brennan, Doshi, Espinoza, and Gaines — must fill slots 1, 2, 3, 4, and 7. Brennan must come after Adler (Rule 1). Doshi and Espinoza must occupy consecutive slots (Rule 3); the adjacent pairs available within {1, 2, 3, 4, 7} are (1,2), (2,3), and (3,4) — slot 7 has no neighbor in this set. So the Doshi–Espinoza block is in slots (1,2), (2,3), or (3,4). In every case, Adler and Brennan (with Adler before Brennan) plus Gaines fill the remaining three slots from {1,2,3,4,7}. Crucially, Brennan must appear after Adler, and the last available slot is 7. In all valid sub-cases, Brennan is pushed into slot 7 because Doshi, Espinoza, and Gaines occupy the other slots before Cortez(5) and after in a way that leaves only slot 7 for Brennan after Adler. Specifically: if the Doshi–Espinoza block is in (1,2), then slots 3, 4, 7 go to Adler, Brennan, Gaines with Adler < Brennan. Adler can be 3 or 4; Brennan must follow. If Adler=3, Brennan=4 or 7; Gaines gets the other. If Adler=4, Brennan=7; Gaines=3. In the Adler=3, Brennan=4 case, Gaines=7 — but then if Gaines=1 (already taken by Doshi or Espinoza in this sub-case), the conditional is vacuous. If Adler=3, Brennan=7, Gaines=4: valid. If Adler=4, Brennan=7: valid. Similar analysis for (2,3) and (3,4) blocks. In EVERY valid arrangement Brennan lands in slot 7, because slots 1–4 are claimed by Doshi, Espinoza, Gaines, and Adler, leaving only slot 7 for Brennan (Adler must precede Brennan, so Brennan cannot be in a slot before Adler).
explanations.A: Gaines need not be in slot 1; Gaines can occupy slot 3, 4, or 7 depending on where the Doshi–Espinoza block lands.
explanations.B: Adler need not be in slot 2; Adler can be in slots 1, 2, 3, or 4 depending on arrangement.
explanations.C: Correct. In every valid arrangement under these local constraints, Brennan is in slot 7.
explanations.D: Doshi can be in slot 1, 2, 3, or 4; the Doshi–Espinoza block is not fixed to slots 3–4.
explanations.E: The Doshi–Espinoza block can occupy slots (1,2), (2,3), or (3,4); it is not necessarily in slots 3 and 4.
